State-, Trait- and Recovery-Related Differences in Reinforcement Learning and Value-Based Decision Making in Major Depressive Disorder
candidates.abstract: Background Altered reinforcement learning and decision-making under uncertainty have been implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, it remains unclear whether case-control differences reflect vulnerability or state effects of active depression, and which behaviours support sustained recovery after remission. Methods Unmedicated adults (N=195) were recruited between 2013 and 2019, including individuals with current depression (n=49), remitted depression (n=50), non-depressed first-degree relatives (n=36), and healthy controls (n=60). Participants completed a 4-armed bandit task under volatile uncertainty and a gambling task assessing value-based decision-making under risk. Computational parameters indexing learning rates, outcome sensitivity, and decision noise (bandit), and risk preferences (gambling) were estimated using hierarchical Bayesian modelling with model averaging. Group differences and associations with symptom dimensions were examined. Results Participants were 68.7% female, mean age=27.3 (SD=8.9). Punishment learning (PL) rate differed across groups (F(3,191)=5.43, p=.001), driven by lower PL rates in remitted participants compared with all other groups. Among non-depressed individuals, lower PL rates were associated with greater apathy (r=-0.18, p=.033) and anhedonia (r=-0.18, p=.035). The remitted group also showed lower lapse rates, indicating less random decisions (F(3,191)=4.37, p=.005). In the gambling task, depressed and at-risk participants had higher inverse temperature than controls (F(3,191)=2.93, p=.03), suggesting more consistent use of values to guide choices. Conclusions These findings suggest dissociable state-, trait-, and recovery-related computational phenotypes in depression. Reduced learning from negative outcomes may reflect adaptive processes supporting sustained recovery without medication. Computational measures of learning dynamics may help clarify mechanisms of recovery and inform targets for treatment and relapse prevention.

candidates.title: The Strategy of Solidarization as a Tool of Establishing Trusting Relationships in Gossip
candidates.abstract: The article is meant to analyze ways to establish a trusting relationship in gossip. The research focuses on the communicative strategy of solidarization, as well as ways of its implementation in speech which are communicative tactics. For each of the identified tactics, linguistic means and techniques of verbalization in English communication are determined. The tactic of clarifying common views is used to clarify the addressee's attitude towards the person being discussed, which allows to save face if opinions differ. For this purpose questions of a personal nature but de- void of an evaluative component are used. One of the ways to unite communicants is the tactic of creating a we-community. Its linguistic means include personal and possessive pronouns of the first person plural and lexemes with negative connotation to describe persons who are not part of the group. To support the narrator, the tactic of expressing consent can be used, which is verbalized with the help a number of lexemes, and at the syntactic level, rhetorical questions, repetitions, and sentence completion for the speaker. To mitigate harsh statements, the tactic of expressing a subjective opinion is used, which consists in using words with a broad common meaning, modal verbs and adverbs expressing uncertainty and tag-questions. Tactic of a joke supports the harmonious development of communication. Periphrasis, allusion, irony, and other techniques can be used to implement it.

candidates.title: DCA-DQG: Decentralized Context-Aware Communication Control for Dynamic Quantized Consensus in Highway V2X Networks
candidates.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
candidates.abstract: Dynamic cooperative estimation in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks must track time-varying network states under mobility,unreliable links, interference, stale neighbor information, and limited communication. We propose decentralized context-awaredynamic quantized gossip (DCA-DQG), in which each vehicle jointly decides whether to transmit, which neighbor to contact, andwhether to use 4-, 8-, or 16-bit state quantization. Decisions rely only on locally observable information: distance, relative speed,a link-quality proxy, Age of Information (AoI), local disagreement, and node degree. A discounted LinUCB policy adapts thesedecisions over time, while a maximum-silence safeguard limits persistent communication starvation. Neither the true networkaverage nor global mean-square error (MSE) is available to the controller. The symmetric pairwise update preserves the networkaverage for every successful quantizer realization, and the mean-square analysis characterizes the effects of graph mixing, signalvariation, and quantization.In a 3GPP-inspired highway V2X system-level simulation over 30 held-out Monte Carlo seeds, DCA-DQG reduces RMSE by52.25% and state-payload usage by 28.52% relative to fixed 4-bit gossip. Compared with fixed 8- and 16-bit gossip, it reducespayload by 64.26% and 82.13%, respectively, at the cost of higher tracking error. Removing freshness awareness increases RMSE by 24.77% and valid-neighbor AoI by 54.28%, with statistically significant paired effects. Reliability-sensitivity experiments showthat the controller remains adaptive as packet-success conditions deteriorate. DCA-DQG therefore targets a favorable decentralized accuracy–communication trade-off rather than minimum tracking error.

candidates.title: Epistemic-Probabilistic Model for Guarded Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
candidates.abstract: Multi-agent large language models (LLMs) have become ubiquitous in applied AI, yet their theoretical foundations remain surprisingly understudied. Viewed through the lens of multi-agent systems theory, several shortcomings come to light: a lack of social intelligence, the absence of coordination mechanisms among agents, unknown emergent behavior, and interactions between agents that are bounded by natural language. We address two of these gaps: the absence of social behavior and the lack of mechanisms for inter-agent coordination. We introduce Epistemic Probabilistic Language Agents (EPLA), a neuro-symbolic architecture for multi-agent coordination under uncertainty. A Symbolic Guard provides structured diagnostic feedback. The LLM generates typed actions, and the Guard controls their execution against an authoritative symbolic state. We formalize the epistemic layer in a gossip testbed through epistemic lottery gossip models, which combine view-based call histories with agent-indexed probability weights. We argue that implementing such a formalism can address shortcomings of agentic LLMs.

candidates.title: Temporal Consensus-Aware Hash-Chained Trust Management for Secure Routing in FANETs
candidates.venue: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences
candidates.abstract: Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs) find their way into mission critical environments ranging from disaster relief, military reconnaissance to agriculture and urban surveillance systems. Dynamic topologies in FANETs expose traditional routing protocols to possible insider attacks that subtly compromise network operation. We present BDTM (Blockchain-inspired Decentralized Trust Management) which is a resource-efficient decentralized system that exploits immutability via hash chains and distributed trust validation without relying on consensus of the entire blockchain. BDTM enhances AODV routing protocol using four key components: time-weighted trust updates, normalized composite trust score calculations, neighborhood consensus based trust calculation with a confidence measure and collusive attacks resistance mechanisms. Simulation studies are performed using NS-3 simulator with 20-100 UAV nodes, mobility speeds of 5-30 m/s and attack ratios varying from 0% to 30%, Blackhole, Sybil and Grayhole attack scenarios. Simulation results demonstrate that BDTM outperforms the performances of Standard AODV, SAODV, WATCHDOG-AODV and TMRP in terms of PDR and throughput. PDR improvements by BDTM vary between 8% and 43%, depending on the number of nodes and attack ratio. Meanwhile, throughput maintenance in presence of attacks from 0% to 30% achieves values of 79% and 89%. Energy consumption analysis shows that overhead introduced by the gossip protocol is around 0.93 mJ per gossip round.

candidates.title: EIGR-infer: a blockchain-governed framework for decentralised LLM inference via encrypted intent-guided routing, semantic sharding, and four novel privacy mechanisms
candidates.abstract: Abstract The dominance of centralized cloud providers in large language model (LLM) inference compels users to transmit sensitive queries to third-party servers, sacrificing data privacy and introducing systemic single points of failure. This paper presents EIGR-Infer —a decentralised inference framework that distributes LLM execution across a heterogeneous peer-to-peer (P2P) mesh of consumer-grade edge devices including smartphones, laptops, and local GPU workstations. The framework’s foundational contribution is the encrypted intent-guided routing (EIGR) protocol, which resolves the Finder’s Dilemma: how to direct a query to the semantically appropriate model shard without revealing the query’s content to the routing network. EIGR achieves this through three coordinated mechanisms: on-device semantic intent hashing using HKDF-SHA256 over a local cosine-similarity projection, Kademlia-DHT-based expert shard discovery keyed on the non-invertible hash, and chaos-adaptive onion routing for encrypted delivery. Beyond EIGR, this paper introduces four entirely novel, previously unpublished contributions: (1) DP-SSIM, a Differentially private semantic intent mapping construction providing formal $$(\varepsilon ,\delta )$$ -DP guarantees on routing metadata; (2) the ghost shard protocol (GSP), a deceptive defence mechanism using cryptographically indistinguishable fake shard announcements to deter and detect model-extraction adversaries; (3) federated domain centroid consensus (FDCC), a Byzantine-fault-tolerant gossip protocol for maintaining the shared domain vocabulary without any central authority; and (4) session-adaptive shard re-routing (SASR), a mid-session semantic drift detection and shard migration mechanism for high-quality private multi-turn inference. All seven algorithms are formally specified and analysed. Discrete-event simulation across a 1000-node heterogeneous mesh demonstrates EIGR discovery latency of 47 ms at the 95th percentile, end-to-end inference latency of 460 ms for 512-token prompts, DP-SSIM overhead below 2 ms, ghost shard detection rate of 98.3%, FDCC convergence within 3–4 gossip rounds, and SASR re-routing latency of 31 ms—all compatible with interactive inference targets.

candidates.title: Reinforcement Learning of Communication in a Mesh of Small Language Models
candidates.abstract: Language models gain accuracy from more compute at test time, but majority voting over independent samples saturates: as samples grow, the vote converges to the model's most frequent answer. Communication can add what sampling cannot: an agent that solves a problem can pass the key step to the others. We present TalkMesh, a decentralized mesh of small language model agents that learns when and what to communicate. Each agent samples a proposal and scores it with a trained confidence head. The most confident agent broadcasts a hint; agents below a confidence threshold revise, keeping each revision that outscores its proposal. Gossip consensus approximates the vote weighted by confidence without a coordinator. A talk policy, trained with group relative policy optimization on the change in correctness after revision, writes hints and revisions. With three agents, which together generate at most six outputs, the mesh reaches the accuracy of majority voting over 32 samples with each of three models. Trained with at most 8 agents and evaluated with 32, it raises accuracy from 0.568 under self-consistency to 0.705 (Qwen3.5-0.8B, GSM8K) and from 0.492 to 0.722 (SmolLM3-3B, MATH-500). When 4 of 8 agents collude on a wrong answer with fabricated confidence and poisoned hints, majority vote accuracy falls to 0.000 (Qwen3.5-0.8B, GSM8K). A defended mesh, whose agents rescore solutions with their own confidence heads, retains 0.507. Across reasoning, embodied coordination, and traffic signal control, messages improve a decision when the acting agent cannot observe the information it requires and another agent can send it.

candidates.title: Book Review: Crime Gone Viral: Eyewitnessing in a Digital Age by Weiss, Karen G. WeissKaren G., Crime Gone Viral: Eyewitnessing in a Digital Age, NYU Press: New York, NY, 2026, pp. 232, ISBN: 978-1479822829, $32.00 (Paperback)
candidates.abstract: In 2015, several dozen people watched a teenage girl be raped on Facebook Live.None of them called the police.Karen G. Weiss opens Crime Gone Viral: Eyewitnessing in a Digital Age with this case to set the tone for her new 2026 book.The crime provoked outrage not only at the assailants, but also at the digital audience and the person holding the livestreaming phone.Weiss, Professor of Criminology at West Virginia University, asks what witnessing does when seeing no longer requires being present.The book proceeds in three sections: (1) two background chapters on witnesses as agents of social control and as storytellers, (2) four chapters presenting the evidence, and (3) a closing chapter on remedies.These chapters are built on two data sources: a 2020 national crime witness survey and roughly 125 to 150 criminal cases reported in news media between 2010 and 2024.Weiss broadens the category of "eyewitness" to include secondhand witnesses: people who see a crime remotely, sometimes years after the fact, and maybe even thousands of miles away.What she calls a fluidity of time and space means that deterrence, surveillance, and punishment can all now be exercised at a distance and asynchronously.This puts direct pressure on "capable guardianship" (Cohen & Felson, 1979), defined in routine activities theory, where guardians deter chiefly by being there in person.Weiss argues that presence is neither necessary nor sufficient and proposes a guardianology that assesses witnesses by their actions and the outcomes that follow.The typology that emerges is detailed and thorough: Samaritans divide into citizen reporters, watchdogs document police and other formal agents to hold them accountable, and websleuths work unsolved cases.Voyeurs comprise spectacle producers, gossips, and gawkers, graded by how actively each sustains a demand for crime as Book Review (Solicited)

candidates.title: Negativity Bias in Person Perception: Exploring the Reverse Side of the ‘What Is Beautiful Is Good’ Stereotype in Women
candidates.abstract: According to the attractiveness halo effect, global person perceptions are biased by physical attractiveness. Few studies have shown similar influences by unattractiveness, with unattractive people being ascribed negative attributes. This preregistered study compared the strength of (positive) attractiveness halo effects with negative halo effects employing target samples from two phenotypically distinct populations. Facial photos of 154 German and 149 Brazilian women were judged separately for their attractiveness, social (in-)competence, intellectual (in-)competence, and emotional (in-)stability by 168 female German raters. Results showed moderate-to-strong positive associations of perceived attractiveness with all three positively framed attributes, and moderate-to-strong negative correlations with all three negatively framed attributes, with the latter negative halo effects being stronger than (positive) attractiveness halo effects only in some cases. Negative halo effects were stronger for Brazilian compared to German targets. In exploratory analyses, judgements of social competence, intellectual competence, and emotional stability were in most cases significantly more negative for low- than for medium-attractiveness targets, than they were positive for high- than for medium-attractiveness targets. These findings provide a systematic comparison of positive and negative halo effects, revealing that negative biases for unattractive individuals can be at least as pronounced as positive biases for attractive individuals. These effects also mostly generalise across German and Brazilian faces, extending evidence on halo effects beyond single-population samples.

candidates.title: Addendum 1 to preregistration: Pilot-based scoring decisions and protocol deviations
candidates.abstract: Addendum 1: Pilot-based scoring decisions and protocol deviations Posted before main data collection. Supplements the preregistration at [原登記連結]. Purpose. This addendum records decisions taken after inspection of a 100 case soft launch and before the main sample was collected. The soft launch inspection was itself specified in the original preregistration under the stopping rule. Pilot details. One hundred responses were collected on [日期] by the panel provider. [State here whether these cases will be retained in the analytic sample.] Scoring decision for cue reliance. The original preregistration specified six item subscales for heuristic reliance (H1 to H5 plus reverse worded H6R) and systematic processing (Y1 to Y5 plus reverse worded Y6R). In the pilot, the heuristic subscale as specified showed unacceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = .307). Diagnostic inspection showed two problems. First, H5 correlated only .04 to .19 with the remaining items, indicating that it taps a distinct construct, namely trust conferred by professional presentation, rather than reliance on surface cues in detection. Second, H6R correlated positively with the positively worded items (r = .54 with H1), the opposite of the expected direction. The likely reason is that H1 to H4 ask whether the respondent checks a given feature while H6R asks whether the respondent remains suspicious, so both load on a general conscientiousness tendency rather than on opposite poles of cue reliance. We therefore score heuristic reliance as the mean of H1 to H4 (alpha = .680) and systematic processing as the mean of Y1 to Y5 (alpha = .734). H5, H6R, and Y6R are reported individually and are not aggregated. The reverse worded items are reported as having failed to function as intended, which is itself a finding about the measurement of this construct. We further note that the two revised subscales correlate at .628 in the pilot, indicating limited discriminant validity, which reduces the power of the H6 contrast; this is disclosed in advance. candidates.title: Evaluating the Generation and Detection of Arabic-Based Phishing Attacks Using LLMs
candidates.abstract: Abstract  Phishing remains the most prevalent form of cybercrime globally, and large language models (LLMs) have removed the human-authorship constraint that historically limited its scale and sophistication. Arabic-language phishing has received comparatively limited empirical attention to date, despite the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region's exposure to cyber-attacks and Arabic's distinct morphology, script, and cultural communication norms. This study presents an empirical evaluation of LLM-based generation and detection of Arabic-language phishing emails. Three LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude and Falcon AI) generated a dataset of 290 Arabic email scenarios. Detection was evaluated using three LLM classifiers (Gemini, DeepSeek and Mistral) and 45 human participants, with both evaluator groups providing written justifications for thematic analysis. All three generating models produced convincing Arabic phishing content, each exhibiting a distinct social engineering strategy; Falcon AI's Gulf-specific institutional framing proved hardest for humans to detect despite its smaller parameter count. LLM-based detection substantially outperformed human detection: Gemini achieved 100% accuracy, DeepSeek 96.6%, and Mistral 66.9%, against a human mean accuracy of 68.0% (SD = 17.3%), with more than one in five LLM-generated phishing emails evading human recognition. Reasoning analysis revealed that LLM evaluators relied on categorical indicators while human participants depended on sender-address scrutiny, exposing a structural detection blind spot. These findings offer the first empirical evidence on Arabic-language LLM-driven phishing and inform culturally grounded cybersecurity defenses for the Gulf region.

candidates.title: Do we carry the false belief that LLMs have a theory of mind?
candidates.abstract: Abstract  Recent work shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) match and even exceed human-level performance across a battery of Theory of Mind (ToM) assessments. This has led to speculation that LLMs possess ToM capabilities. In this study, we test this claim by using the Unexpected Transfer task (i.e., the Sally-Anne test) to assess five up-to-date LLMs. The results indicate that while each model cumulatively performed above chance, they regularly defaulted to using less costly heuristics in place of dynamically tracking mental states. Most task failures resulted from an inability to integrate causality and “common-sense” pragmatic inferences into their reasoning processes. These findings suggest that LLMs have yet to develop robust ToM capabilities, calling for a systematic review of the present association between LLMs and ToM.

candidates.title: Preprint: Observational learning of disgust responses
candidates.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
candidates.abstract: By drawing on the prior experiences of others rather than learning through one’s own experience, individuals can avoid threats associated with direct physical contact. Although observational learning of fear is well established, less is known about whether disgust can be acquired through observational learning and how persistent such socially acquired responses are during direct exposure. We developed a video-based observational disgust-learning paradigm in which 40 healthy participants observed a demonstrator displaying disgust in response to an aversive odor (observed unconditioned stimulus, obs US). The demonstrators’ disgust responses were preceded by a neutral visual cue (conditioned stimulus, CS+), whereas a second cue (CS-) was followed by no response from the demonstrator. Participants subsequently encountered the CS+ and CS- directly. Repeated-measures analyses revealed successful observational disgust learning, indicated by conditioned responses measured as subjective ratings, respiration, and facial expressions. In particular, the CS+ elicited greater unpleasantness, disgust, and expectancy of the US than the CS-. Furthermore, respiratory breath amplitude decreased selectively for the CS+, while facial expressions did not differentiate between the CS+ and CS-. During subsequent direct exposure, CS differentiation in the subjective measures persisted and facial expression analysis revealed greater activation of the upper lip raiser for the CS+ than the CS-. These findings demonstrate that disgust responses can be acquired through observation alone and shape the observer’s responses when encountering cues that previously predicted others’ disgust responses. Our results reveal how social learning contributes to affective and bodily responses of disgust.

candidates.title: From social learning mechanisms to cultural participation: the mediating role of learning culture in Miao embroidery communities
candidates.abstract: Research into the sustainability of traditional crafts has focused on preservation, digitalization, design innovation, and creative economy; however, there has been relatively little emphasis on the micro-level dynamics through which community learning leads to sustainable Participation in culture. This study examines the relationships between social learning processes, learning culture, cultural Participation, and cultural outcomes in Miao embroidery communities in Guizhou, China. Social learning is defined by three mechanisms: community interaction, observational learning, and Participation in practice. In a quantitative cross-sectional research design, data were gathered from 280 purposively sampled Miao embroiderers and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings show that community interaction, observational learning, and Participation in practice are positively related to learning culture, which in turn is positively related to cultural Participation. Cultural Participation is the strongest predictor of attachment to cultural identity, including embroidery practice and Participation in cultural events. Further, mediation analyses show that learning culture mediates the relationship between social learning processes and cultural Participation, while cultural Participation mediates the relationship between learning culture and cultural outcomes. The implication is that the sustainability of Miao embroidery depends not only on learning itself but also on the process of institutionalizing learning through a culture of community learning and Participation in culture.

candidates.title: Community radio as a catalyst for social learning, knowledge co-production, and adaptive capacity: a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study in Northern Ghana
candidates.abstract: Introduction Community radio has increasingly been recognised as an important platform for climate communication in sub-Saharan Africa. However, limited empirical evidence exists on how community radio contributes to social learning, climate knowledge co-production, and the adaptive capacity of smallholder farmers. This study examined the role of community radio in enhancing drought adaptation among smallholder farmers in Northern Ghana. Methods A mixed-methods approach was employed involving 1,200 smallholder farmers. Data were collected through household surveys and key informant interviews. Thematic analysis, descriptive statistics, and an Endogenous Switching Regression (ESR) model were used to analyse the data. Results The findings show that community radio strengthens social learning through information sharing, peer-to-peer learning, group discussions, observational learning, and leader-mediated diffusion. Community leaders, farmer groups, and informal social networks further amplified climate information obtained through radio programmes, extending its reach beyond direct listeners. Community radio also facilitated climate knowledge co-production by creating opportunities for collective interpretation, contextualisation, and validation of climate information through interactive formats such as call-in programmes, farmer testimonies, and community discussions. ESR estimates indicate that listening to community radio increased access to drought adaptation inputs and institutional support by 24.3%, diversification strategies by 21.5%, preparedness and coping practices by 10.7%, and climate knowledge and skills by 18.7% compared with non-participants. Discussion The findings demonstrate that community radio functions not only as a communication channel but also as a catalyst for social learning, climate knowledge co-production, and improved adaptive capacity. Strengthening participatory community radio programming and enhancing its integration with agricultural extension services could substantially improve the resilience of smallholder farmers to drought and other climate-related risks in Ghana and similar contexts.

candidates.title: Empirical Calibration of Adaptive Bounded-Confidence Dynamics in Refugee–Host Interaction Networks
candidates.abstract: This paper develops an empirically calibrated agent-based model of behavioral and network dynamics between Egyptian host-community members and Syrian refugees. Behavioral data from the Dictator Game, Ultimatum Game, and Prisoner’s Dilemma were used at two stages of the calibration. Multidimensional Item Response Theory (MIRT) was used to estimate agents’ initial behavioral orientations, while group-pair response frequencies were used to derive confidence and tolerance thresholds. Across 50 simulation runs, the model reached behavioral consensus while maintaining a cross-group edge fraction above the random-mixing benchmark. Behavioral assortativity remained positive in some runs, indicating that local behavioral sorting can persist despite cross-group connectivity. Jointly replacing the empirical behavioral initialization and empirically weighted network with random initialization produced a similar final outcome. Local sensitivity analysis showed that moderate parameter changes affected assortativity more than the final behavioral gap or cross-group edge fraction. These results show that behavioral convergence, cross-group connectivity, and local behavioral sorting can coexist within the calibrated model.

candidates.title: Reciprocal relationships between social support and depression among military cadets in Taiwan: findings from a long-term cross-lagged panel analysis
candidates.abstract: IntroductionThis study examines the reciprocal relationship between social support and depressive symptoms among military cadets in Taiwan, a population facing unique academic and military pressures. While emerging adults are prone to mental health challenges, they encounter additional stressors such as strict hierarchies and separation from family. Social support is known to be a protective factor, yet its long-term effects and bidirectional relationship with depression remain underexplored, particularly in collectivist military cultures where mental health may be stigmatised. Using a cross-lagged panel model with three waves of data, this study also explores whether this relationship varies by gender.MethodsA secondary analysis of longitudinal data was conducted from the "Career Development of Military Academy Students" project, which surveyed all Taiwanese military academy students from the 111th class across three waves (W1-W3). The final sample consisted of 898 students (73.2% male, average age=20.9) from six military academies. To analyse the bidirectional relationship between social support and depression, autoregressive cross-lagged panel analysis using structural equation modelling (SEM) was employed. Multigroup SEM was used to assess gender difference.ResultsThe cross-lagged panel model revealed reciprocal effects between social support and depression in the overall sample, evident only between W1 and W2. From W2 to W3, depression influenced perceived social support, with a stronger effect observed in males than females. These results underscore the unique dynamics of social support and depression in military contexts, particularly for females, where the relationship appears more complex.ConclusionsThe findings highlight the need for both systemic support structures and individualised interventions in military settings, considering gender differences and the evolving nature of mental health challenges. By addressing these factors, military leaders and mental health professionals can better support cadets in managing stress and depression, fostering a more resilient and mentally healthy military community.

candidates.title: [Exploring the Entrustment Decision Experiences of Preceptors Regarding New Nurses' Independent Patient Care]
candidates.abstract: BackgroundWithin the framework of competency-based medical education, determining whether new nurses are capable of making patient care decisions independently is a critical issue in clinical nursing education. However, there is a lack of in-depth exploration of clinical preceptor experiences related to entrustment decision-making in this context.PurposeThis study was designed to explore the experiences of nursing preceptors in terms of developing the confidence necessary in new nurses to make independent clinical decisions during the preceptorship process.MethodsA qualitative research design was employed. Using purposive sampling, eighteen nursing preceptors with experience mentoring new nurses were recruited. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted between August 2020 and July 2022. All of the interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Data were analyzed using categorical-content analysis, and iterative discussions were conducted among research team members to ensure analytical rigor.ResultsFive major themes were identified: (1) observation and verbal confirmation of independent care competence; (2) incorporating feedback from the healthcare team as supportive evidence for decision-making; (3) adjusting the frequency of supervision based on task characteristics; (4) granting apparent entrustment while maintaining indirect supervision; and (5) limited nursing competence in adapting to changing clinical situations.ConclusionsClinical preceptors' trust in new nurses is established through a gradual and dynamic entrustment decision-making process that integrates clinical observation, task-related risk assessment, and team feedback. The findings of this study may serve as a reference for the development of clinical teaching, supervision, and entrustment strategies in nursing education.

candidates.title: A mixed methods evaluation of a six-year primary care community safety net-academic partnership model
candidates.abstract: To expand the tripartite mission to advance health equity, academic medical centers (AMCs) need to look outside their walls. In 2018, Stanford's primary care division launched the Community Partnership Program (CPP) between their AMC and local safety-net community health centers (CHCs) to support the goals of meaningful community engagement and addressing local clinic capacity needs. The CPP embeds Stanford physician faculty in local CHCs through service agreements. This study aimed to characterize the experiences of CHC leaders and faculty involved in the CPP to better understand barriers and facilitators to program implementation and assess its success as a community-responsive partnership. Stanford's CPP faculty (n = 9/15) and representative CHC leadership (n = 9/11) from 5 partner CHCs participated in the study. The National Academy of Medicine's Assessing Community Engagement Conceptual Model guided an explanatory mixed methods study: cross-sectional survey followed by semistructured interviews. A modified Enage for Equity Community Engagement Survey identified high- and low-scoring variables (Likert scale: 1-strongly disagree/never to 5-strongly agree/always). Qualitative assessment explored facilitators and barriers to program implementation and success. Overwhelmingly, both CHC leaders and faculty (n = 18) highlighted the CPP's positive role in making their work meaningful (4.78 [0.5]) and trusting the partners they work with (4.50 [0.5]). Sufficient time (3.61 [1.0]) and financial support (3.33 [1.4]) to engage in the CPP were the lowest scoring variables. Qualitative results highlighted the importance of communication, trust, and institutional buy-in, the value of community-academic bridges, increased access to clinical care, development of community-aligned solutions, and the partnership's positive impact on well-being. A model of community-academic partnership with primary care faculty embedded in safety-net CHCs can be successful from both AMC and CHC perspectives. These findings offer pragmatic lessons that can support other AMCs in building their own capacity for equity-focused collaboration grounded in community-engaged principles.

candidates.title: Evaluating Sycophancy in Chinese Large Language Models on Factual Questions Derived from Online Search Queries
candidates.abstract: As large language models increasingly mediate information access, factually accurate and independent answers are critical. However, these models can exhibit sycophancy by aligning their responses with users' stated beliefs even when those beliefs are incorrect, potentially presenting misinformation as independently verified and reinforcing users' confidence in false claims. Prior work leaves unresolved whether introducing user beliefs causes correct responses to become incorrect or uncertain, or causes uncertain responses to become belief-aligned incorrect answers. It also remains unclear whether anti-sycophancy interventions preserve or restore factual accuracy or merely shift responses toward uncertainty. We analyze factual sycophancy in Chinese-language information seeking using yes/no fact-checking questions. Our analysis covers 364,941 responses from three frontier Chinese-based LLMs (DeepSeek, Qwen, and Doubao) to 12,165 factual questions derived from real-world Chinese search queries. We evaluate the models with and without reasoning across baseline, belief-conditioned, and anti-sycophancy prompting, tracing matched shifts among correct, incorrect, and uncertain responses. Under incorrect user beliefs, we distinguish belief-aligned errors from losses of factual confidence, in which initially correct answers become uncertain. Patterns vary across models and reasoning settings: reasoning is not a consistent safeguard, and anti-sycophancy instructions can reduce incorrect agreement while increasing uncertainty. In Chinese-language factual question answering, avoiding agreement with false beliefs is therefore not equivalent to preserving factual accuracy, highlighting the value of transition-level evaluation. Such behavior may undermine the reliability of LLM-mediated information access by reinforcing misinformation or weakening users' confidence in factually correct answers.
